item.title: Anyone can be the best depending on how structural variant callers are evaluated
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79601-7

An evaluation of long-read structural variant detection methods shows that reported performance can depend strongly on how they are evaluated, highlighting the need for more consistent benchmarking practices.
item.dc:title: Anyone can be the best depending on how structural variant callers are evaluated

item.title: Identification and functional characterization of bacterial bilirubin vinyl reductase across vertebrate gut microbiomes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79675-3

Here, the authors identify a gut bacterial enzyme, bilirubin vinyl reductase (BilV), showing it is complementary to bilirubin reductase (BilR) and required to reduce bilirubin into urobilinogen, an essential step in the heme degradation pathway.
item.dc:title: Identification and functional characterization of bacterial bilirubin vinyl reductase across vertebrate gut microbiomes

item.title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79635-x

Huang et al. show that canted magnetization in SrRuO3 generates a sizable out-of-plane damping-like torque without relying on low crystal symmetry, offering a strategy toward scalable magnetic-memory devices with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.
item.dc:title: Control of out-of-plane anti-damping spin torque with a canted ferromagnetic spin source

item.title: Rigidity-driven molecular assembly for high-efficiency flexible perovskite/CIGS tandems
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79826-6

Flexible perovskite and copper indium gallium selenide tandem solar cells are hindered by rough interfaces that reduce efficiency and stability. Yao et al. designed a rigid molecular contact enabling efficient, durable devices that withstand prolonged operation and bending.
item.dc:title: Rigidity-driven molecular assembly for high-efficiency flexible perovskite/CIGS tandems

item.title: The human hypothalamus encodes prediction errors during sensory–nutrient inference
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79339-2

How neural circuits compute nutrient content from sensory cues is not fully understood. This study shows that oral texture shapes how people judge the fat content of foods and identifies hypothalamic signals when texture and fat content mismatch, linking these neural signals to fat intake.
item.dc:title: The human hypothalamus encodes prediction errors during sensory–nutrient inference

item.title: A membrane-active cationic supramolecule to treat both fungal and bacterial keratitis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79812-y

In this work, authors report a membrane-active cationic supramolecule, Y8, with potent cross-kingdom activity against vision-threatening fungal and bacterial keratitis. It is ocular-compatible and outperforms or matches standard therapies in animal models.
item.dc:title: A membrane-active cationic supramolecule to treat both fungal and bacterial keratitis

item.title: Buried stochastic interfaces enabling depth-multiplexed optical physical unclonable functions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79605-3

Optical physical unclonable functions often rely on surface-accessible features. Here, the authors conceal stochastic nanotexture at vertically stacked silicon interfaces beneath a planarized surface and use depth-selective optical gating to read eight planes for reliable hardware authentication.
item.dc:title: Buried stochastic interfaces enabling depth-multiplexed optical physical unclonable functions
item.dc:creator: Taeyeong Kim
Kibum Jung
Jungchul Lee

item.title: Transcriptional nodes governing diversity and effector rewiring of a plastic liver invariant natural killer T cell ecosystem
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78497-7

The transcriptional diversity of liver-resident invariant natural killer T (LiNKT) cells remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors map eight mouse LiNKT cell subsets and show how transcription factors guide their conversion into inflammatory or regulatory states, revealing targets for controlling liver inflammation and repair.
item.dc:title: Transcriptional nodes governing diversity and effector rewiring of a plastic liver invariant natural killer T cell ecosystem

item.title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79694-0

Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma is an aggressive childhood cancer commonly driven by H3K27M with few treatment options. This study links H3K27M-driven chromatin remodelling to NFI-dependent purine metabolism, causing ATIC/PNP-mediated metabolic rewiring and ATIC-targetable tumour dependence.
item.dc:title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma

item.title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79550-1

Plant cells are encased in cell walls that when digested leave spherical protoplasts. Here the authors report long, thin membrane protrusions from protoplasts termed phytopodia and discuss their potential role in the probing behaviour of the cell cortex.
item.dc:title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
